title: Page document
description: One page: its title and search description, and a tree of blocks. The tree is strict: the page holds sections, a section holds one to four columns, a column holds widgets, a widget holds nothing. Every block has the same five keys {id, type, props, children, style}. The editor (ajv) and the server (json_schemer) validate against this same file; schema/README.md lists what it cannot express and where that lives instead.
$comment: Dispatch is if/then on the type const, never oneOf. Patterns use only explicit ASCII classes and \u escapes, so ECMA-262 and json_schemer's ECMA translation read them the same way. Engines: ajv Ajv2020 {strict:true, strictTuples:false, allErrors:true, validateFormats:false, unicodeRegExp:true}; json_schemer {regexp_resolver:'ecma', format:false}.

schemaVersion.description: Raised on every change of shape; older documents are upgraded when read.

title.description: Shown in the browser tab and in search results.

description.description: Shown under the title in search results. Absent when the page has none.

sticky.description: The site's header's: it stays at the top of the window while the page scrolls under it. Only true is stored; a page's or a footer's is not read.

blockType.description: Every block type. A new widget is added here, to widgetType, and as one if/then branch of block.

widgetType.description: The block types a column may hold: every block type except section and column.

block.$comment: The dispatcher. The five keys are declared here, so additionalProperties sees them whichever branch runs. The enum on type is what stops an unknown type: it would match no 'if' and pass unchecked. 'required: ["type"]' inside each 'if' stops a block without a type from matching every branch.

sectionBlock.description: A band of the page. Its column count is the number of its children, one to four; there is no separate count to keep in step. Side by side on desktop, the columns share the width equally unless columnWidths names a preset for that many columns; on tablets and phones they stack, unless stack says otherwise.

label.description: Shown only in the editor, in the navigator and in history.

sectionBlock.$comment: Which presets a section may name depends on how many columns it holds: one branch per count, keyed on the length of children (the lint checks that every count has one, and that each preset has as many parts as its branch has columns). A section of one column has nothing to share or to stack, so it names neither a preset nor where to stack. The 'properties: {columnWidths: true}' beside each 'required' under 'not' only declares the key for ajv's strictRequired.

columnBlock.description: One column of a section. It holds widgets only, never another section or column.

videoBlock.description: Stored as provider and video id, never as a URL: the renderer builds the player address from the provider's fixed pattern, so no stored string is parsed as a URL on the way out.

title.description: The player's accessible name, and the caption of the click-to-load card.

mapBlock.description: Stored as coordinates; the renderer builds the map address.

icon.description: A name from the project's own icon set (schema/icons.svg): the site's eight, then forty of Lucide's under their Lucide names; both renderers draw it from that set. Never markup or a URL.

statsBlock.description: Figures side by side, each a short value (12, 300+, 98%) and the label that says what it counts. The value is text, written as it is shown.

items.description: The figures, in the order the page shows them.

stepsBlock.description: Numbered steps in order, each a title and a short text: what to do first, then next. The page numbers them; the number is not stored.

items.description: The steps, in the order the page numbers them.

pricingBlock.description: Plans side by side, each a name, a price as it is written and what it is for, a short text, what it includes and a button. A plan may be featured: the page rings it and shows its badge.

plans.description: The plans, in the order the page shows them.

formBlock.description: A form a visitor fills in and sends, with no script: its fields in order, the text of its button, and the message shown once it is sent. The fields live here, in the page's version, and nowhere else; each answer the server keeps records the version it was sent from and a copy of its fields.

items.description: The fields, in the order the page shows them. Their names are unique in the form: an application rule, since uniqueItems compares whole fields.

confirmation.description: What the visitor reads once the server has kept the answer.

logoBlock.description: The site's mark, the theme's own drawing. With a name, the mark and the name beside it are a link to the home page, as a header has them; without one, the mark alone, which a screen reader skips, as the design's footer has it. On a dark band (a background of the text or primary slot) the mark draws itself the other way round. mark false draws the name alone, a word mark, as a site of its own has it; a logo with no name draws the mark whatever mark says.

mark.description: false: the name alone, without the theme's mark. Only false is stored.

menuBlock.description: The site's links in a row, which fold into Menu, a disclosure that opens them as a sheet with no script, wherever the block is narrower than the row needs. A published page cannot measure itself, so the server works that width out from the widths of the labels' letters (HeaderFit) and the block names the step it folds below. label names the menu for a screen reader (Main, Footer): two menus of one page need two names.

items.description: The links, in the order the row shows them.

collectionListBlock.description: The published entries of a collection, each a card that links to its entry's page: as many as count, in an order, those whose choice or toggle field holds a value when it filters, laid out as a list, a grid or a compact list, each card showing its title and the fields it names. Which entries those are is data of the CMS's: the renderers are given them. A collection that is not there, or one with nothing to list, draws what emptyText says.

collection.description: The collection, by its id; absent until one is chosen.

layout.description: list: one card under another, its image beside its words; grid: cards side by side, as many as columns, its image above; compact: a title and a day a line, no image, no excerpt.

columns.description: How many cards a row of the grid holds at most; read by the grid only.

image.description: The image field a card shows, by its key.

date.description: The date field a card shows, by its key.

excerpt.description: The text or paragraph field a card shows under its title, by its key.

price.description: The number field a card shows as a price, by its key: in the shop's currency when it is the price of the collection the shop sells from while the shop is on, as a number otherwise.

linkLabel.description: The words at a card's foot (Read more), or none.

emptyText.description: What the list says when it has no entry to show.

fieldBlock.description: A value of the entry a collection's template is drawn with: its title, or one of its collection's fields by its key, drawn as the field's type draws it (a text as a heading of level when it names one, else as a paragraph; a paragraph's lines; the rich text; the image; the day; a link as a button; a toggle that is on as its field's label; a choice's option; a number as written). Only a template holds one, an application rule of the editor and the CMS outside this file; anywhere else, and for a value the entry has not, it draws nothing.

field.description: The field's key, or title for the entry's own title.

level.description: A text drawn as a heading, of this level; absent, as a paragraph. Read for a text and the title only.

addToCartBlock.description: A form that puts the entry a collection's template is drawn with in a visitor's cart: it posts the entry and a quantity to the cart's own address, with no script, and its button is a button block's, its words and its colours. Only a template holds one, an application rule of the editor and the CMS outside this file. It draws for an entry of the collection the shop sells from, while the shop is on; for a product out of stock or with no price it says so where its button goes, and is no button; anywhere else it draws nothing. Which entry it is, and whether it is for sale, are the CMS's data: the renderers are given them.

label.description: The button's words, as a button block's.

quantity.description: Whether the form asks how many, from 1 to 20, beside its button; without, it puts one in.

listOrder.description: The order a collection list puts its entries in: by when they went live (publishedAt), by title, or by the key of one of its collection's date or number fields; ascending or descending. An entry with nothing to order by comes last.

listFilter.description: Only the entries whose choice field holds this option, or whose toggle field is on or off: the field by its key, and the value.

fieldKey.description: A field of a collection, by the key its values are kept under: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, as an anchor (collection.schema.json's fieldKey, which is never title or slug).

pricingPlan.description: One plan of a pricing block. Its price is text, written as it is shown (with its currency, or Free), never a number the page would format, and its period says what the price is for (a month), or is empty. Its text, its period and its badge are always there and may be empty; its features are lines, none to twelve; its button is a button block's words and link, by a button block's own rules. Its badge is drawn only while it is featured.

features.description: What the plan includes, one line each, in the order the page lists them.

button.description: The plan's button: a button block's label and href, by the same definitions.

menuLink.description: One link of a menu: its words and where it goes, by the link rules of a page.

formField.description: One field: a line of text, an email address, a longer text, or a checkbox; its label, whether it must be filled in (a checkbox: ticked), and for the two kinds of text the most characters an answer may have.

name.description: The key its answer is kept under, the same from one version to the next while the field stays. Made by the editor, never shown: a label can change and the answers still line up.

maxLength.description: Characters, as code points: at most 300 for a line of text, 5000 for a longer one. An email address takes the standard's 254, and a checkbox has no text.

formField.$comment: One if/then per kind on maxLength, with the same 'properties: {x: ...}' beside each 'required' as imageRef, for ajv's strictRequired.

imageRef.description: One image: from the media library ({mediaId}) or from another site ({url}), never both. It has alt text, or is marked decorative and has none. Each gallery item has this shape, and the image widget's props have it with the block's class and anchor (imageProps).

imageProps.description: The image widget's props: one image as imageRef has it, and the block's class and anchor.

decorative.description: Only true is stored: an image that adds nothing for a screen reader. Absent means the image needs alt text.

imageRules.$comment: Exactly one source and exactly one of alt or decorative, written with if/then/else rather than oneOf, for imageRef and imageProps alike. The 'properties: {x: true}' beside each 'required' only declares the key for ajv's strictRequired; it checks nothing.

sectionPicture.description: A picture of the media library behind a section, covering it: one setting for every device, as an image block's source is. The page draws it as the section's first child, decorative (its words say what matters, and its alt text is empty), cropped to the section's box around the point its style's focus keeps in view, under the veil its style's veil and veilStrength give it, so the words over it read. A library item only, by its mediaId, which counts as a use of the item as an image's does; an item the library no longer has draws no picture, and no veil.

noChildren.description: Widgets hold no blocks: children is always the empty array.

anchor.description: In-page link target: #anchor scrolls to the block, whose element on the page has it as its id. Unique on the page, and none in the site's header or footer: application rules.

className.description: CSS classes of the site's own, which its custom CSS can style: one to eight names, each a letter then up to 39 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, one space between two. The names the theme uses are refused by an application rule.

mediaId.description: The public id of a media library item. The renderers resolve it to a file address.

line.description: A single line of plain text with at least one visible character.

paragraph.description: Plain text that may hold line breaks (\n only), with at least one visible character.

lineOrEmpty.description: A single line of plain text, or nothing: a field that is always there and may be left empty, never blank. Once it holds anything, it has a visible character, as a line does; ^$ is the whole value, empty.

paragraphOrEmpty.description: Plain text that may hold line breaks (\n only), or nothing: a field that is always there and may be left empty, never blank. Once it holds anything, it has a visible character, as a paragraph does.

lineControls.$comment: Used under 'not'. Unanchored on purpose: it finds a control character anywhere, so a field stays closed even if json_schemer is set back to its Ruby resolver, where ^ and $ match at every line break.

paragraphControls.$comment: Used under 'not': like lineControls, but a line feed is allowed.

href.description: A link target: https or http with a host (no user info), mailto:, tel:, a site path (/..., never //host), a ?query or a #fragment. ASCII only: the editor percent-encodes anything else.

imageUrl.description: An image from another site: https with a host (no user info), or a site path. No http (mixed content), no data:, no //host.

spaceToken.description: Spacing steps, the keys of space.site in tokens.json (None to XXL in the editor).

sectionSpaceToken.description: The space above or below a section's content: a spacing step (the keys of space.site in tokens.json) or a section step (the keys of space.site-section). Absent, a section takes the theme's rhythm for the device.

columnWidthsToken.description: How a section's columns share the width wherever they are side by side, as parts in column order: 3:2 gives the first column three fifths. fit is a column as wide as what it holds, and the columns with parts share what is left: fit:1:fit is a header's mark, links and button. Absent, they share it equally; equal is never written. Which presets a section may name depends on its column count (sectionBlock): two columns 3:2, 2:3, 2:1, 1:2, fit:1 or 1:fit, three columns 2:1:1, 1:2:1, 1:1:2 or fit:1:fit, one and four columns none.

stackToken.description: Where a section's columns go one under the other. Absent, below the desktop layout, on tablets and phones; phone, on phones only; never, on no device, as a header's mark and links stay on one row. A section of one column names none.

aspectToken.description: The shape an image is cropped to, the keys of aspect.site in tokens.json: width to height, or original for the image's own shape.

paletteSlot.description: The six palette slots of the site style. A block names a slot, or a free colour of its own (freeColor): the site owner picks the tone of each slot, and every block that names it follows.

backgroundToken.description: A palette slot, or none for no background.

freeColor.description: A colour of the site's own choosing, where a block's colour or background names one instead of a slot: six lowercase hex digits after #, the one way it is written.

typeStep.description: Steps of the site type scale, from type.site in tokens.json.

veilToken.description: The veil over a section's picture, so the words over it read: none; dark, a neutral black; light, a neutral white; text, the site's Text tone. The words take the colour that reads on it, as on a band: the site's Background tone on a dark veil and on the Text tone's, its Text tone on a light one, headings, links and icons with them. Absent, none. Read only while the section draws a picture.

veilStrengthToken.description: How much the veil hides the picture: light, medium or strong. Absent, medium.

focusToken.description: The point of a section's picture kept in view where the section's box crops it: its centre, the middle of an edge, or a corner. Absent, the centre.

motionToken.description: How a block comes into view as the page scrolls to it: none; rise, up from a little below; fade; zoom, from a little smaller. Drawn by the stylesheet alone, with no script (a scroll-driven animation), and only where the browser can play it and the visitor has not asked for less motion: anywhere else the block is simply there. Absent, none.

typefaceToken.description: The face a heading, a text or a quote is set in: the body's or the headings'. Unset, a heading takes the headings' face, a text and a quote the body's.

fontSize.description: A heading's, a text's or a quote's own type size, over its step's: the number and its unit as one string, in px, rem or vw, with two decimals at most and written one way only, no zero before the number but the one before a point and none ending its decimals (48px, 2.5rem, 0.75vw). How far each unit goes is an application rule (sizeRange): 8 to 320 px, 0.5 to 20 rem, 0.5 to 25 vw. A vw is a hundredth of the page's width, which the renderers write as a hundredth of the page root's (cqw), so the canvas draws it as the page does.

fontWeight.description: Its own weight, over its typeface's: 100 (Thin) to 900 (Black), in steps of 100. The headings' face draws every one; the body's goes from 200, and draws 100 as 200.

letterSpacing.description: Its own letter spacing, in em, from -0.1 to 0.5, with two decimals at most (an application rule, decimals).

lineHeight.description: Its own line height, a multiple of its size, from 0.8 to 3, with two decimals at most (decimals).

letterWidth.description: How wide its letters are drawn, a percentage of the typeface's width axis, from 62.5 to 125, with two decimals at most (decimals). Only the headings' face, Archivo, has that axis: in the body's it changes nothing.

styleTokens.description: Every style setting: a token name, or a free colour (freeColor) for a background or a colour, or a free value for type (fontSize, fontWeight, letterSpacing, lineHeight, letterWidth), each over what the tokens give. In tablet and phone an absent key means 'as on desktop' (base); there is no null.

style.description: base applies everywhere; tablet and phone hold only what differs there. An override that is removed is a key that disappears, and an empty override object is not stored.

sectionStyle.description: Section: its background, and over a picture of its own (sectionPicture) the veil, its strength and the point kept in view; the space above, below and between its columns; how it comes into view; whether it is shown. The picture's settings are read only while the section draws one. Every block's style takes motion.

textStyle.description: Heading, text and quote: their step of the type scale and their typeface, and over those, free type of their own (a size, a weight, letter spacing, a line height, a letter width), each key over the step's or the face's on its own; their colour, where they stand, how they come into view, and whether they are shown.

statsStyle.description: Stats: the colour of their figures' values, where each figure's words stand, and whether they are shown.

stepsStyle.description: Steps: the colour of the discs their numbers stand in, and whether they are shown.

pricingStyle.description: Pricing: the colour of the featured plan's ring and its badge, and whether it is shown. The plans' words keep the band's colour.

collectionListStyle.description: Collection list: the colour of its cards' words, and whether it is shown.

fieldStyle.description: Field: the settings of the widget it draws as, a heading's or a text's for words (their step, typeface, free type, colour and alignment), an image's crop, a button's colours and alignment, and whether it is shown. Each is read only while the field draws as that widget, and kept while it does not.

navStyle.description: Logo and menu: the colour of their words, where they sit in their column, and whether they are shown.

lineStyle.description: Divider and accordion: the colour of their lines.

imageStyle.description: Image: its crop, which may differ per device, and whether it is shown. The crop is a style setting, not a property, because it is what changes from one device to another, like a text size: the approved page crops its hero image square on desktop, 16:9 on tablets and 5:4 on phones.

plainStyle.description: Spacer, video, map and form: how they come into view, and whether they are shown, per device.

pmDoc.description: Rich text as the editor's getJSON() gives it, cut down to paragraphs, line breaks, bullet and numbered lists, and bold, italic and link marks.

pmListItem.description: A list item starts with a paragraph; nested lists and further paragraphs follow.

pmMarks.description: Each mark at most once on a node. Two links on one run of text would be one <a> inside another, which HTML does not allow and a browser splits in two; the editor's marks each exclude themselves, so it never writes a repeat.
pmMarks.$comment: 'Not two of a type', written with contains and minContains: 2 under not, because uniqueItems would compare whole marks (two links to different addresses are different items) and is not used here anyway (see the lint).

pmMarkLink.description: The attrs the editor's link mark writes. Only href carries meaning: the renderers set target and rel themselves.
